Care that feels steady and practical

I’m {{THERAPIST_NAME}}, a licensed clinician ({{LICENSE}}) working with adults to navigate anxiety, overwhelm, relationship shifts, and life transitions. I blend evidence-informed techniques with pragmatic tools so you can build daily practices that support sustainable change.

{{PRIMARY_CTA_LABEL}}
{{THERAPIST_NAME}}, {{LICENSE}}
Based in {{CITY}}, {{STATE}} • {{MODALITIES}}

My story — why I do this work

I came to therapy because relationships felt hard and deadlines felt relentless. Over the years I trained in trauma-informed care, cognitive-behavioral therapies, and somatic awareness. That mix helps me support people in both understanding patterns and developing practical, daily moves that create more ease.

I aim to hold sessions that are warm, clear, and grounded in real life. Sessions are collaborative: we set goals together, track small changes, and adjust based on what actually helps you feel safer and more capable.

Values in practice
Confidentiality, clarity, and consent are central. I will explain limits of confidentiality, document collaboratively, and invite your questions about treatment direction and boundaries.
Ethics & scope
I work with adults on mood, anxiety, trauma recovery, relationship concerns, and life transitions. I do not provide emergency services; if you are in crisis, please call local emergency services or a crisis line.

How I structure work — a simple framework

1. Map & Orient

We start by clarifying what matters most to you now and forming humane, measurable goals.

2. Learn & Practice

We introduce skills to shift patterns (emotion regulation, grounding, relational skills) and practice them in-session.

3. Integrate

We focus on everyday routines so gains hold when sessions end.

4. Review & Transition

We check progress, plan maintenance, and create a transition plan when you’re ready.

Programs I offer

Grounding Sessions — Single Consult

60-minute focused session for specific challenges or initial assessment.

Roots — 8-session package

A short-term, skills-based package for anxiety and transition work with measurable steps.

Bridge — monthly continuity

Ongoing weekly or biweekly sessions for deeper relational or trauma work; we review regularly and adapt.

Community referrals

I can help coordinate with psychiatrists, support groups, and allied professionals when needed.

What people notice

"I left sessions feeling clearer and with practical steps I could try the next day — warm and actionable." — A.
"A steady presence that helped me slow down and notice what I actually needed." — J.

Fees & how to book

Standard session

Typical 50–60 minute session. Packages available for discounted sequencing.

Sliding options

A limited number of reduced-fee spots are available; please inquire via email.

To book: {{PRIMARY_CTA_LABEL}} or call {{PHONE}}

Confidentiality & privacy: Sessions are confidential except where required by law (e.g., imminent risk of harm, mandated reporting). Please ask for a copy of the privacy practices.
Scope & boundaries: I provide psychotherapy for adults. I do not offer emergency services. If you are in crisis, call local emergency services or a crisis hotline.

Areas I commonly support

I work with adults navigating life transitions, persistent anxiety, and complex relational patterns. Below are common themes I support — each card notes what to expect and how we pace the work.

{{PRIMARY_CTA_LABEL}}

Anxiety & Worry

Practical pacing, skills for uncertainty tolerance, behavioral experiments. Often 6–12 sessions to build foundational practices.

Trauma-related distress

Safety first: stabilization, grounding, and gradual processing when appropriate. Work is collaborative and paced to your tolerance.

Relationship patterns

Explore attachment, communication patterns, and boundary-strengthening. Sessions include in-the-moment skill practice.

Burnout & work transitions

Practical strategies to rebuild energy, examine expectations, and design sustainable routines.

Life transitions

Starting/stopping relationships, moving cities, career shifts. We focus on values, meaning, and practical adjustments.

Grief & loss

Compassionate support for processing loss, finding ways to carry memories, and returning to daily functioning when ready.

How I tailor work

I integrate cognitive-behavioral strategies, somatic awareness, and relational repair. We co-create a plan that honors your pace and capacity; nothing is mandated. If work falls outside my scope I'll help with referrals.

"I valued the balance of practical tools and being heard — sessions helped me change small habits that made a big difference." — M.

Access & fees

I offer single sessions, short-term packages, and limited reduced-fee spots. Insurance may be accepted depending on plan—please inquire. To check availability or ask about fit, {{PRIMARY_CTA_LABEL}} or email {{EMAIL}}.

Confidentiality note: Records are kept securely. There are legally required exceptions to confidentiality; feel free to ask for details. For crises, call emergency services or your local crisis line.

Home About Areas Fees Contact

Evidence-informed, person-centered practice

My approach blends practical skill-building with attention to safety and relationships. I aim to offer sessions that feel grounded, collaborative, and useful in everyday life.

Licensed: {{LICENSE}} {{PRIMARY_CTA_LABEL}}

Therapeutic frame

I begin with safety and stabilization. From there we learn practical tools (breathing, grounding, thought experiments) and experiment with small behavioral changes. Over time we integrate those practices into daily routines so progress is sustainable.

Core influences

  • CBT and ACT for thinking and behavior shifts
  • Trauma-informed stabilization and somatic awareness
  • Relational repair and communication skills

How sessions typically flow

  1. Check-in & symptom tracking
  2. Brief skills practice or experiential work
  3. Review homework & plan next steps

Sessions are collaborative; you set the pace. Progress is tracked in concrete ways so we can see what helps.

{{THERAPIST_NAME}}, {{LICENSE}}
Modalities: {{MODALITIES}}
Single session
A focused 50–60 minute meeting. Useful for short-term tools or assessment.
Short package
8-session block for skills work and habit integration.
{{PRIMARY_CTA_LABEL}}
Boundaries & safety

I am not available for crisis management. Confidentiality is prioritized; exceptions include imminent harm, abuse reporting requirements, or legal orders. If you are in immediate danger, call emergency services.

Therapy pathways — how we might work together

Discovery Session

Single consult to clarify goals and fit.

Stabilize & Skill

4–12 sessions focused on safety, regulation, and skill practice.

Continuous Support

Ongoing weekly or biweekly sessions for long-term or complex concerns.

Client commitments

Therapy is most helpful when sessions are regular, homework is attempted between sessions, and feedback is shared openly. If you need to pause or change frequency, we will plan that together.

A brief note on limits

I do not give medical or emergency services. If you are experiencing suicidal intent or immediate danger, please call emergency services or a crisis hotline. For medication questions, I can coordinate with prescribers but do not prescribe myself.

To inquire: {{EMAIL}} • {{PHONE}}
